title: Deciding to leave Hampton in 1947 and planning to rest
summary: After a Pittsburgh Courier night at Carnegie Hall, Cobb resolves to leave, using his back as an excuse, after the Wantz brothers book him for Easter and Gladys objects that it didn't come through her.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, okay, so now you leave Lionel for the (inaudible), and you form your small band. Is that it?

Yeah. I tell you what -- I played a Pittsburgh Courier thing at Carnegie Hall with him at midnight and we received awards, and I was in the running of the saxophone players for the Pittsburgh Courier. And, of course, we had to stay up until 8:00 o'clock that morning going into Columbus, and this is when I made up my mind I was going to put my notice in.

So I knew what the situation was in the band. I'm giving it to you just like it is. I told my wife, I say, I'm coming home, because things wasn't right in the band, see. Duke was in on this situation, and I'd been a victim of circumstance. So I told Duke, I said, Duke, I think I'm going to have to leave the band. My back is giving me a lot of trouble, and my doctor said I'm going to have to come off the road. My doctor didn't say nothing.
Well, (inaudible) excuse me for a second. Your back was giving you a lot of trouble at this point?
It was before. You know, I told you that.
You got that on tape already.
He told them that. This is the excuse he was saying.

I told you it was giving me trouble, but after I'd gone to California I was getting all right then, but not all right either in a sense of the word, so I thought if I just take off about six months -- I'll give you a thing that happened. We was in Philadelphia at the Earl Theater and the Wantz Brothers came over to me and talked to me about working that club, and I knew we was going to be off at Easter, so they were going to work me two weeks. And I took it for the money that they was going to pay me because I'd planned to leave anyway. So that gave me time to put my notice.

But, see, Gladys went over -- when they told Gladys and Hamp when they went over to the club they was hiring me on that for Easter, Gladys said, you didn't come through me. And they come back and told -- I said, come through her? I wasn't working there. We off Easter. Thought they going to dominate my life. I won't be there anyway. This is why I leave. Nobody knows but me and my wife, why I left.
So, okay, Duke and I stay together, and we catch the train going on to Columbus at 8:00 the next morning. We

didn't go to bed after the show. I get to the house where we're going to stay. Hawk is a tourist. Gladys stayed there (inaudible). And I told Duke, I said, I'm going to have to leave today. I said, my doctor told me I'm going to need some rest. Now, I ain't seen my doctor. But I'm planting a seed now.

And he goes upstairs to take a bath, and I called my wife and tell her, I'm coming in (inaudible), and that's going to be it because I'm putting my notice in when we opened the theater tomorrow here. She said, come on in. Well, he come on back downstairs. We get to the theater and we opened up, and Joe Morris come to me after the first show, say, what is this, you leaving the band? I ain't told Hamp yet, because I didn't put my notice in until I got to Cleveland.
But I told Duke, I said --
